title: The root-to-fifth distance
summary: Give a familiar distance a name.

steps.title: The root-to-fifth distance
steps.body:
**interval** means the distance between two notes. A **perfect 5th** is an interval of seven half steps. G to D spans five letter names: G, A, B, C, D. **perfect** is the name for this plain form of the interval.

**Why it matters:** This open, stable distance gives you a useful second sound to put above a root.

steps.title: Read the positions
steps.body: Start with G2 at string 6, fret 3. D3 is seven half steps higher: string 6, fret 10, or string 5, fret 5. Both places give the same D3. Play G, then D, one at a time.

items.prompt: Play G2, then go up a perfect 5th.

steps.title: Make it comfortable
steps.body: Compare the distance on one string with the shorter route across two strings. Do not stretch your fingers to reach both frets on one string at once.

items.prompt: How far apart are these two notes?
Play A2, then go up a perfect 5th.
